_comment: Chapter 1 scene texts. Quoted verses come from verses.json (a published translation), not from this file.

lines: I don't understand what's happening to me. But I have to get out.
This street… this sky… This isn't the neighbourhood I know.
Everything is still. And there's no one here.
The path goes on above the clouds. From stone to stone…
The souk… but no one. That noon light that never moves.
Time has stopped here.
Gold, everywhere… Would I only have to follow it?
It's dark. But the pages shine.
Outside… the sky has changed again.
The higher I climb, the closer the sky.
Up there, a door of light. Like a dawn that is waiting.
Heedless… turned away.
That's me. That is what ghafla is.
Last night the Mushaf was right there, on the shelf. And I didn't even open it.
I can't stay like this. I will find every page.
anbiya.objective: Find the pages of the Mushaf. Some of them hide.

lines: Al-Fatiha… Seventeen times a day, in my obligatory prayers.
How many times did I truly mean it?
All that time spent chasing money…
It ran away from me, and I kept following it. It slipped through my fingers.
I counted my gains. I never counted my days.
Al-Kahf… On Fridays.
I used to read it every week. Then one Friday missed, then another…
I regret those empty Fridays so much.

pool: One more page. It lights up the cave.
Young men taking refuge with their Lord… and I took refuge in sleep.
Every Friday I read it. Until I stopped.
I recognise these words. They come back to me, page after page.
Here, time doesn't count. That is exactly the problem.
It glows as if it were waiting for me.

lines: The last page of the cave.
Hoping to meet my Lord… and I slept right beside His word.
As-Sajdah… It went with Al-Mulk, every evening before sleep.
How many evenings did I miss that appointment?
Al-Mulk… I used to read it every evening before sleeping.
Last night I went to bed without it.
The last three… The ones for the morning, for the evening, for before sleep.
The sun is already up. But the door back is not closed.
I must get up, make my ablutions, and pray.
Horses charging at full gallop… and what was I charging after?
I was ungrateful without even noticing.
On that day there will be no more time to waste.
And I have wasted so much, on trifles.
Time… I let it slip away.
I counted my riches, never my days.
But it is not too late to begin again.
The time I wasted chasing money, no one will give back to me.
I believed that hoarding would protect me.
All their strength was powerless against what He had decided.
And I relied on my own means.
